question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Apple)

calls.reasoning: Anchor: Apple guided FQ4 FY26 revenue growth of 9-11% YoY on 102.466B, which is 111.7-113.7B. The guidance included a 2.5pt FX headwind and supply constraints that 'increase significantly'. Recent record: guided 14-17% for the June quarter and delivered 16.4%; FQ4 FY25 guided 5-8% and delivered 7.9%; FQ1 and FQ2 FY26 landed at or above the top of their ranges. So Apple usually lands in the upper part of its range or beats it. Consensus is about 113.3B (MarketBeat) to 114.3B (another source). Pulling the other way: Nikkei reports Apple cut iPhone 18 Pro orders by 15-20% on soft demand after a $100 price hike. Only the launch weeks fall inside the September quarter, though, and the higher prices help average selling price. Supply limits also cap any big beat. Median is about 113.45B, near the top of the guide. Market check: no Polymarket, Kalshi, or Manifold contract found for Apple's revenue figure.
calls.dossier:
- Apple's FQ4 FY26 (September quarter) guidance, given Jul 30 2026: total revenue up 9-11% YoY on the prior-year 102.466B, which works out to about 111.69-113.74B. FX is a ~2.5pt sequential headwind. Supply constraints on iPhone, Mac and iPad are expected to 'increase significantly' from the June quarter. iPhone growth guided to mid-teens, Services growth 'largely similar' to the June quarter's 12% after adjusting for FX, gross margin 47-48% (Fool transcript, Aug 2026).
- FQ3 FY26 (June quarter) actual: 109.417B, +16.4% YoY, against guidance of 14-17% given Apr 30 2026 (CNBC; 9to5Mac Jul 30 2026). iPhone 54.25B, +22%.
- FQ2 FY26 actual 111.184B, +16.6% YoY. FQ1 FY26 actual 143.756B, +15.7%. FQ4 FY25 actual 102.466B, +7.9% against guidance of 5-8%. Over the last ~4 quarters, results landed at the top of the guided range or above it.
- Consensus revenue for the quarter: about 113.31B per MarketBeat (Oct 2026), about 114.3B per another aggregator cited in an iGeeksBlog article (Oct 2026).
- Nikkei/MacRumors (Oct 9 2026): Apple cut iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max component orders 15-20% after a $100 price hike (starting at $1,199/$1,299) to offset memory costs. Demand was softer from late August into October. Only the launch weeks fall inside the September quarter.
- 9to5Mac (Oct 14 2026): a separate report says Apple is gearing up for strong iPhone 18 sales, so the reports conflict.
- IDC projects 2026 worldwide smartphone shipments down 16.7%, citing the memory shortage.
- Status quo: the result lands near the top half of the guided range, as in recent quarters.
- Resolves off the total net sales Apple reports in its FQ4 FY26 earnings release (8-K), expected Nov 2 2026 after market close. Initial figure only.
- Event window: the September quarter ended ~Sep 26 2026; the figure is released Nov 2 2026. As of Oct 25 the quarter is 100% complete, and only the release is still pending.
- Searched for but did not find: any Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on Apple's revenue; whisper numbers; exact iPhone 18 launch-week sell-through data.

calls.reconciliation: Disputes: (1) FQ4 FY25 guidance range (5-8% vs 8-10%) — factual, unsettleable without web; both agree actual ~+8%, so it was at or near guide either way and does not change the pattern of at-or-above-top results. (2) Beat magnitude — judgment: Run 3's $114.0B median extrapolates unconstrained-quarter beats; Apple's own 'significantly greater' supply constraint language and the short launch window argue for a smaller beat, so median near guide top ~$113.6B. (3) iPhone 18 Pro demand reports conflict (Nikkei cuts vs JPM) — judgment, small impact on Sept quarter. Carried Run 2's dispersion basis forward. No market exists per all runs.
